title: Open-Source Essential Mathematics for the Victorian Curriculum Year 8

chapters.title: Integers and the Number System
chapters.description: Operations with directed numbers, order of operations, powers and roots of integers, and mathematical modelling with integers in Australian contexts.

sections.title: Adding and Subtracting Integers
sections.vcaa_description: Use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing efficient strategies, including using the properties of operations and mental, written and digital strategies, and make estimates to check reasonableness.
sections.target_mastery: Accurately add and subtract positive and negative integers using number lines, directed number rules, and associative/commutative properties.
prerequisites: Locating positive and negative integers on a horizontal or vertical number line (Year 7 VC2M7N05)
Adding and subtracting whole numbers fluently
sub_concepts: Opposite integers and additive inverses
Adding and subtracting a positive integer on a number line
Adding and subtracting a negative integer (equivalent sign rules)
Multi-step integer sums and Australian temperature/elevation contexts

sections.title: Multiplying and Dividing Integers
sections.vcaa_description: Use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing efficient strategies, including using the properties of operations and mental, written and digital strategies, and make estimates to check reasonableness.
sections.target_mastery: Multiply and divide positive and negative integers fluently, including powers with negative integer bases.
prerequisites: Multiplication tables up to 12 x 12 and short division
sub_concepts: Sign rules for multiplying two integers
Sign rules for dividing two integers and undefined division by zero
Products of three or more directed numbers
Integer powers of negative bases: (-a)^n versus -a^n

sections.title: Order of Operations and Directed Numbers
sections.vcaa_description: Use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing efficient strategies, including using the properties of operations and mental, written and digital strategies, and make estimates to check reasonableness.
sections.target_mastery: Evaluate multi-step arithmetic expressions involving brackets, indices, multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction with integers.
prerequisites: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing integers (Sections 1A-1B)
Order of operations with positive whole numbers
sub_concepts: Brackets and nested grouping symbols (parentheses, square brackets, fraction bars)
Indices (exponents) and roots in expressions
Left-to-right precedence for multiplication/division and addition/subtraction
Estimation and checking reasonableness in applied problems

sections.title: Lowest Common Multiple, Highest Common Factor, and Prime Factorisation
sections.vcaa_description: Establish and apply the exponent laws with positive integer exponents and the zero-exponent, using exponent notation with numbers.
sections.target_mastery: Express composite numbers in prime factor form using exponent notation and use prime factorisation to determine HCF and LCM.
sub_concepts: Factor trees and prime factorisation in index form
Determining the Highest Common Factor (HCF) via prime factors
Determining the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) via prime factors
Applications of HCF and LCM to scheduling and packaging problems

chapters.title: Fractions, Decimals, Irrational Numbers and Index Laws
chapters.description: Rational and irrational numbers, terminating and recurring decimals, operations with positive and negative fractions/decimals, and index laws.

sections.title: Operations with Positive and Negative Fractions
sections.vcaa_description: Use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing efficient strategies.
sections.target_mastery: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide positive and negative fractions and mixed numerals.
prerequisites: Equivalent fractions and lowest common denominator
sub_concepts: Adding and subtracting signed fractions
Multiplying signed fractions and cross-cancelling
Reciprocals and dividing signed fractions

sections.title: Terminating and Recurring Decimals
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise terminating and recurring decimals, using digital tools as appropriate.
sections.target_mastery: Convert between fractions and terminating or recurring decimals using dot and bar notation.
sub_concepts: Terminating decimals and prime factors of denominators (2 and 5)
Recurring decimal notation (dots and vinculum)
Ordering rational numbers

sections.title: Irrational Numbers and the Real Number System
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise irrational numbers in applied contexts, including square roots and pi, and recognise that real numbers comprise rational and irrational numbers.
sections.target_mastery: Classify numbers as rational or irrational, evaluate or estimate square and cube roots, and work with exact values involving pi and surds.
sub_concepts: Rational vs irrational numbers
Estimating non-perfect square roots between consecutive integers
Pi as an irrational ratio in geometry

sections.title: Index Laws and the Zero Exponent
sections.vcaa_description: Establish and apply the exponent laws with positive integer exponents and the zero-exponent, using exponent notation with numbers.
sections.target_mastery: Simplify numerical expressions with exponents using multiplication, division, power of a power, and zero-index laws.
sub_concepts: First Index Law (multiplying same base)
Second Index Law (dividing same base)
Power of a power law
The Zero Index Law (a^0 = 1)

chapters.title: Percentages and Financial Mathematics
chapters.description: Percentage conversions, percentage increase/decrease, Goods and Services Tax (GST), discounts, profit and loss, and simple interest.

sections.title: Percentages, Percentage Change and GST
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate percentage increases, decreases, and 10% Australian GST inclusive and exclusive prices.
prerequisites: Converting between fractions, decimals, and percentages
sub_concepts: Percentage of a quantity
Multiplier method for percentage increase and decrease
Australian 10% GST calculations (finding pre-GST price by dividing by 1.1)

sections.title: Profit, Loss, Discounts and Simple Interest
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Solve financial modelling problems involving mark-ups, discounts, percentage profit/loss on cost price, and simple interest I = Prt.
sub_concepts: Profit and loss as a percentage of cost price
Successive discounts
Simple interest formula I = Prt

chapters.title: Ratios, Rates and Best Buys
chapters.description: Simplifying ratios, dividing quantities in a given ratio, scale drawings, unit rates, speed, and unit pricing.

sections.title: Simplifying Ratios and Dividing in a Ratio
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios, rates and scale.
sections.target_mastery: Simplify ratios involving whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and different units, and divide quantities into a given ratio.
sub_concepts: Simplifying ratios to simplest whole-number form
Unitary method and total-parts method
Map scales and scale factors

sections.title: Rates, Speed and Best Buys
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise and use rates to solve problems involving the comparison of 2 related quantities of different units of measure.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate and convert rates including average speed, fuel consumption (L/100 km), and supermarket unit pricing ($/100g).
sub_concepts: Unit rates and comparison shopping
Average speed, distance, and time
Converting between m/s and km/h

chapters.title: Algebraic Techniques
chapters.description: Algebraic substitution, collecting like terms, multiplying/dividing algebraic terms, expanding brackets, and factorising linear expressions.

sections.title: Language of Algebra, Substitution and Like Terms
sections.vcaa_description: Create, expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying the associative, commutative, identity, distributive and inverse properties.
sections.target_mastery: Substitute directed numbers into algebraic expressions and simplify expressions by collecting like terms and multiplying/dividing pronumerals.
sub_concepts: Terms, coefficients, and constants
Substitution with negative values
Collecting like terms
Multiplying and dividing algebraic terms

sections.title: Expanding Brackets and Factorising Linear Expressions
sections.vcaa_description: Create, expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying the associative, commutative, identity, distributive and inverse properties.
sections.target_mastery: Apply the distributive law to expand brackets and factorise linear expressions by extracting the Highest Common Factor (including negative factors).
sub_concepts: The distributive law a(b + c) = ab + ac
Expanding and simplifying with negative multipliers
Factorising by extracting the algebraic HCF

chapters.title: Linear Equations and Coordinate Graphs
chapters.description: Solving multi-step linear equations, equations with brackets and pronumerals on both sides, plotting linear graphs, gradient, and y-intercept.

sections.title: Solving Linear Equations
sections.vcaa_description: Solve linear equations and verify solutions by substitution.
sections.target_mastery: Solve two-step and multi-step linear equations, including equations with brackets, fractions, and pronumerals on both sides.
sub_concepts: Inverse operations and maintaining balance
Equations with brackets and algebraic fractions
Equations with pronumerals on both sides
Checking solutions by substitution

sections.title: Graphing Linear Relations and Modelling
sections.vcaa_description: Graph linear relations on the Cartesian plane; use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving linear relations.
sections.target_mastery: Plot linear relations on the Cartesian plane, determine gradient and y-intercept from y = mx + c, and model real-world linear relationships.
prerequisites: Plotting points on the 4-quadrant Cartesian plane
sub_concepts: Tables of values and plotting straight lines
Gradient (rise over run) and y-intercept
Finding the rule y = mx + c
Linear modelling in real-world contexts

chapters.title: Length, Area, Volume and Time
chapters.description: Circumference and area of circles and sectors, area of special quadrilaterals and composite figures, volume and capacity of prisms, and Australian time zones.

sections.title: Perimeter and Area of Quadrilaterals and Composite Shapes
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the area and perimeter of irregular and composite shapes using appropriate units, including choosing between metric units of area.
sections.target_mastery: Convert between metric area units (mm^2, cm^2, m^2, ha, km^2) and calculate the area of parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombuses, kites, and composite shapes.
sub_concepts: Metric area unit conversions (including hectares)
Area formulas for parallelogram, trapezium, rhombus, and kite
Composite areas by addition and subtraction

sections.title: Circumference and Area of Circles and Sectors
sections.vcaa_description: Demonstrate how the formulas for the circumference and area of a circle are established, and use them to solve practical problems.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate exact and rounded values for the circumference and area of circles, quadrants, semicircles, and sectors.
sub_concepts: Circumference C = 2*pi*r = pi*d
Area of a circle A = pi*r^2
Perimeter and area of sectors and composite circular shapes

sections.title: Volume, Capacity of Prisms and Time Zones
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the volume and capacity of right prisms using appropriate units; solve problems involving duration and time zones.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate the volume of right prisms using V = Ah, convert between volume (cm^3, m^3) and capacity (mL, L, kL), and solve Australian/global time zone problems.
sub_concepts: Volume of right prisms V = Ah
Volume and capacity equivalence (1 cm^3 = 1 mL, 1 m^3 = 1000 L)
Australian time zones (AEST, ACST, AWST and Daylight Saving AEDT/ACDT)

chapters.title: Pythagoras' Theorem and Geometry
chapters.description: Pythagoras' theorem, congruent and similar triangles, properties of quadrilaterals, 3D coordinates, and geometric algorithms.

sections.title: Pythagoras' Theorem
sections.vcaa_description: Use Pythagoras' theorem to solve problems involving the side lengths of right-angled triangles.
sections.target_mastery: Apply a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find the hypotenuse or a shorter side in right-angled triangles, identify Pythagorean triads, and solve practical problems.
sub_concepts: Identifying the hypotenuse and stating a^2 + b^2 = c^2
Finding the hypotenuse vs finding a shorter side
Pythagorean triads and converse test for right angles

sections.title: Congruence, Similarity and Quadrilateral Properties
sections.vcaa_description: Identify the conditions for congruence and similarity of triangles and establish properties of quadrilaterals.
sections.target_mastery: Use the four congruence tests (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS) to prove triangles are congruent and deduce angle and side properties of special quadrilaterals.
prerequisites: Angle sum of triangles and quadrilaterals
sub_concepts: Triangle congruence tests (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS)
Similar figures and scale factors
Deductive proofs of quadrilateral properties and decision algorithms

chapters.title: Probability and Venn Diagrams
chapters.description: Complementary events, two-way tables, Venn diagrams, tree diagrams, and experimental probability simulations.

sections.title: Complementary Events, Venn Diagrams and Two-Way Tables
sections.vcaa_description: Determine all possible combinations for 2 events, using two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams, and use these to calculate probabilities.
sections.target_mastery: Use complementary events Pr(A') = 1 - Pr(A), construct and interpret Venn diagrams and two-way tables, and calculate compound probabilities (AND, OR, NOT).
sub_concepts: Complementary events and sum of probabilities
Venn diagrams (intersection, union, mutually exclusive events)
Two-way tables and tree diagrams

chapters.title: Statistics and Data Analysis
chapters.description: Census vs sampling, bias, frequency tables and histograms, mean, median, mode, range, and the effect of outliers.

sections.title: Data Collection, Summary Statistics and Outliers
sections.vcaa_description: Analyse and report on the distribution of data from primary and secondary sources using summary statistics and displays, describing the effect of outliers.
sections.target_mastery: Distinguish between census and sample, calculate mean, median, mode, and range from raw data and frequency tables, and explain how outliers affect measures of centre.
prerequisites: Mean, median, mode, and range of small data sets
sub_concepts: Census vs sample and sources of sampling bias
Calculating mean, median, mode, and range from frequency tables
Effect of outliers on the mean versus the median
